course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

quiz.title: Unit 2 FRQ 4: Modeling a non-periodic context (Topics 2.9 to 2.15)
quiz.headline: Build a logarithmic model from two data points, interpret an average rate of change, and judge a long-range prediction.
quiz.promptTitle: Free response 4 · Modeling a non-periodic context · graphing calculator
quiz.prompt: A greenhouse records the height of a seedling, in centimeters, t days after it sprouts. The height is modeled by H(t) = a + b log₂ t for t ≥ 1, where a and b are constants. On day 2 the seedling is 9 centimeters tall, and on day 16 it is 21 centimeters tall.
quiz.instructions: Part A style: a graphing calculator is required. Show the work that leads to each answer; answers without supporting work may not earn credit where work is requested. Avoid rounding intermediate values, and give decimal approximations accurate to three places after the decimal point unless the part says otherwise. Unless otherwise specified, the domain of a function f is the set of all real numbers x for which f(x) is a real number.
quiz.note: Original practice question written in the AP Precalculus free-response format (6 points, parts A to C). Scoring is self-assessed with the point-by-point rubric. It is not an official AP question or an official AP score.

scaffold.label: Show work
scaffold.text: Write the setup, such as the expression you evaluate or the equation you solve, before the answer.

scaffold.label: Use notation
scaffold.text: Use limit notation, interval notation, and units exactly where a part asks for them.

scaffold.label: Justify
scaffold.text: When a part says give a reason or explain, refer to the given values or the context.

responseFields.label: Part A (i)
responseFields.prompt: A (i). Use the given data to write two equations that can be used to find the values for constants a and b in the expression for H(t).
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part A (ii)
responseFields.prompt: A (ii). Find the values for a and b.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part B (i)
responseFields.prompt: B (i). Use the given data to find the average rate of change of the height of the seedling, in centimeters per day, from t = 2 to t = 16 days. Express your answer as a decimal approximation. Show the computations that lead to your answer.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part B (ii)
responseFields.prompt: B (ii). Interpret the meaning of your answer from part B (i) in the context of the problem.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part C (i)
responseFields.prompt: C (i). Use the model to find the value of t, in days, at which the seedling is 30 centimeters tall. Express your answer as a decimal approximation.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part C (ii)
responseFields.prompt: C (ii). The plant species never grows taller than 35 centimeters. Is the model H appropriate for predicting the height of the plant one year (365 days) after it sprouts? Give a reason for your answer.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

rubric.label: A (i) Two equations
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for a + b log₂ 2 = 9 and a + b log₂ 16 = 21, or the equivalent a + b = 9 and a + 4b = 21.

rubric.label: A (ii) Values of a and b
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for a = 5 and b = 4.

rubric.label: B (i) Average rate of change
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for (21 − 9)/(16 − 2) = 12/14 ≈ 0.857 centimeters per day, with the computation shown.

rubric.label: B (ii) Interpretation
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for: from day 2 to day 16, on average, the height of the seedling increased at a rate of about 0.857 centimeter per day. The interval, 'on average', and units are needed.

rubric.label: C (i) Value of t
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for 5 + 4 log₂ t = 30 with t = 2^(25/4) ≈ 76.109 days.

rubric.label: C (ii) Reason
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for: no, because H(365) ≈ 39.047 centimeters, which is greater than 35, since a logarithmic model increases without bound while the plant's height is limited to 35 centimeters.

quiz.modelResponse:
A (i). H(2) = 9 and H(16) = 21 give a + b log₂ 2 = 9 and a + b log₂ 16 = 21, that is, a + b = 9 and a + 4b = 21.

A (ii). Subtracting, 3b = 12, so b = 4 and a = 5. H(t) = 5 + 4 log₂ t.

B (i). (H(16) − H(2))/(16 − 2) = (21 − 9)/14 = 12/14 ≈ 0.857. The average rate of change is about 0.857 centimeters per day.

B (ii). From day 2 to day 16, on average, the height of the seedling increased at a rate of about 0.857 centimeter per day.

C (i). 5 + 4 log₂ t = 30, so log₂ t = 25/4 and t = 2^(25/4) ≈ 76.109 days.

C (ii). No. The model gives H(365) = 5 + 4 log₂ 365 ≈ 39.047 centimeters. A logarithmic model increases without bound, but the plant never grows taller than 35 centimeters, so the model overestimates the height for large t and is not appropriate at t = 365.
quiz.alternateModel: In C (ii) it is also correct to find when the model reaches 35 centimeters, at t = 2^7.5 ≈ 181.019 days, and explain that predictions after that day exceed the plant's maximum height.
commonErrors: Writing a·b log₂ t or solving for b as 12.
Giving 12 centimeters, the change, instead of dividing by 14 days.
Claiming the model is appropriate because logarithmic functions grow slowly, without comparing H(365) to 35.
